newsitem.title: UK: BARCLAYS SEES NO RECESSION FROM RATE RISE.
newsitem.headline: BARCLAYS SEES NO RECESSION FROM RATE RISE.

text.p: British bank Barclays does not believe the latest rise in UK interest rates to seven percent will lead to a recession but does expect growth to slow in 1998.

"We're not concerned about a recession next year though there may be lower growth," Barclays chairman Andrew Buxton told reporters at a news conference. "We are much more concerned that inflation should be controlled."

Barclays chief executive Martin Taylor said rates at the current level, they have risen from six percent to seven percent via four quarter point rises, would not have a significant impact on the bank's business.

Buxton, who is also chairman of the Confederation of British Industry's economic affairs committee, said the macroeconomic policies being pursued by Britain's Labour Party government are very similar to those seen under the previous Conservative Party administration.

"The policy...is to keep inflation down using monetary policy and to keep the economy stable," Buxton said. "That seems to be a good policy and good for our business. Our business thrives on stability for our customers."
